sections.h2: Where do you file a deed in Hocking County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Hocking County deeds go to the ground-level office inside the courthouse at 1 East Main Street, Logan. Mail goes to P.O. Box 949, Logan, OH 43138. The recorder's page gives 740-385-2031 for the office and 740-385-0377 for fax.

Two clocks apply. Visitors are welcome until 4 in the afternoon, but recording stops at half past three, the same cutoff as copy requests, and the research room shuts at 3:45. In bad weather the office opens at 10 a.m. under a Level 2 snow advisory and stays closed under Level 3, so phone before driving in from the Hocking Hills side.

The index covers records from 1818, the year the county was organized, and electronic indexing began on January 1, 1992. Logan is the county seat. Buchtel, Laurelville and Murray City, the county's three villages, use the same counter.

sections.h2: How much does the Hocking County Recorder charge?
sections.html:
The county posts its own fee sheet. Recording costs a flat $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after, and the sheet says the price includes a $5 restoration fee.

Hocking County Recorder fees as the county prints them
ServiceCharge
Recording, first two pages$39
Recording, each page after$8
Marginal reference$4 each
Document that breaks the layout rules$20
Print made in the office$1 a page
Print made by staff, or an emailed copy$2 a page

The office does not run title searches, give legal advice or prepare documents. Have the deed drafted ahead of time by your closing agent or lawyer. Recording payments can be made at the counter, and the recorder's page also links an online payment portal and a land records search.

sections.h2: What layout rules apply to a Hocking County deed?
sections.html:
The recorder's page explains that House Bill 525 created the layout standards, now section 317.114 of the Revised Code, effective July 1, 2009. A deed that falls short costs $20 more. What counts as conforming:

  • Type of 10 point or larger, in black or blue ink, with no highlighting anywhere.
  • One inch of margin on both sides and the bottom of each sheet.
  • Three inches clear at the top of page one for the recorder, auditor and engineer, and an inch and a half on later pages.

Court and taxing authority papers, plats, DD-214 discharges, state or federal documents and anything signed before the law took effect are outside the rule. A deed you draft yourself is not.

sections.h2: What kinds of papers does the Hocking County Recorder file?
sections.html:
The county's list is long, and a seller's file may touch several items on it. Deeds can be warranty, quit claim, survivorship or sheriff's deeds. Mortgage papers include releases, assumptions, assignments, subordinations and waivers of priority. The office also files certificates of transfer, affidavits, easements, leases, land contracts, plats, condominium records, powers of attorney and trusts.

Liens deserve a second look because a title search will find them. The list names these:

  • Mechanic's liens and notices of commencement.
  • Federal tax liens and personal tax liens.
  • Workers' compensation and unemployment compensation liens.
  • Child support liens and Medicaid fraud liens.

A seller who knows of one should say so early. The list also shows that annexations, street name changes and vacated streets and alleys are recorded here, which can affect a rural lot's frontage.

sections.h2: What does the Hocking County Auditor handle on a transfer?
sections.html:
The auditor sees the deed first and collects the Ohio conveyance fee, so call 740-385-2127 for the figure on your sale price. The auditor's tools menu includes a calculator that adds a parcel transfer fee to its answer. Ask at the same time whether the county levies a real property transfer tax, since that is optional for each county.

A January 2026 message on the auditor's site says short-term rentals are now valued apart from residential property, at their market value as short-term rentals. Anyone selling a cabin near the state park should ask how the parcel is classified before quoting taxes to a buyer.

The same message says the budget commission, commissioners and township trustees trimmed inside millage so collections stayed near the 2024 level after the 2025 valuation update. Without that, the auditor estimates the county's inside millage would have drawn about $1.25 million more, a 22% increase.

sections.h2: How can a Hocking County owner reduce or contest a tax bill?
sections.html:
The treasurer's page on reducing taxes lists several routes. The owner occupancy credit, once called the 2 1/2% reduction, requires that you own the home, live in it as your main residence, and apply with the auditor between January 1 and the first Monday in June. It excludes rentals, corporate or partnership owners, units in commercial buildings, taxed manufactured homes and acreage beyond one acre.

Disagreeing with the value? The Board of Revision, made up of the treasurer, the auditor and the president of the commissioners, hears appeals filed with the auditor from January 1 through March 31. The best evidence is a recent sale price shown by closing papers, or sales of comparable homes, plus photographs of the property's condition.

A late-payment penalty can be removed on request for these reasons:

  • The owner never received a correct bill and tried to get one.
  • The payment was mailed by the due date with a proper postmark but never processed.
  • Serious injury, death or a hospital stay within 60 days before the due date, with payment inside 60 days after it.
  • An error by the auditor or treasurer.
  • Reasonable cause without willful neglect, for owners timely in each of the last three years.

sections.h2: How do taxes and the land bank touch a Hocking County sale?
sections.html:
The Hocking County Treasurer is in Suite 201 of the courthouse, phone 740-385-3517. The treasurer's page says new legislation pushed the 2026 second-half collection date for real estate and mobile homes to August 7, 2026. That date has passed, so anyone who sold around it should ask the treasurer to confirm that both halves posted.

The auditor describes five state tax bills signed December 19, 2025. House Bill 186 raises the owner occupancy credit from 2.5% toward 15.38% by tax year 2029 and phases out the 10% non-business credit, and House Bill 335 slows growth in inside millage to the rate of inflation. Most of that shows up on bills from 2027 on.

The county also runs a land bank. Its page says the bank acquires vacant, abandoned and tax-foreclosed properties, waives delinquent taxes on property it takes, and deed-restricts residential parcels to prevent nightly rentals. Owners of worthless or low-value parcels can offer them to the bank instead of leaving them to a tax foreclosure.

The land bank page also says the bank is governed by a five-member board that includes the county treasurer, two commissioners, the mayor of the largest municipality and one member with real estate experience. Residential houses it sells go to buyers who show a need for single-family housing and agree to owner-occupy.

sections.h2: Which Hocking County housing figures help set a price?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts Hocking County at 27,512 people in July 2025 and 13,024 housing units. Its 2020 to 2024 survey shows owners in 78.8% of occupied homes, a typical home value of $186,400, typical rent of $808 and household income of about $62,960. The average commute runs 30.3 minutes, the longest among the three counties in the Census table used for this region.

About 70.6% of residents lived in rural areas in 2020, and a piece of the Wayne National Forest and Hocking Hills State Park both fall inside the county line. The Hocking River drains about half the county, and Salt Creek drains much of the southwest.

Lodging and restaurant sales of roughly $89 million in 2022 were the highest of the three counties, which points to a visitor economy. A seller near the park should not assume every buyer wants a year-round home.

faqs.q: How much is a Hocking County recording?
faqs.a: A flat $39 covers the first two pages, and each extra page adds $8, including a $5 restoration fee. A deed that breaks the layout rules adds $20.

faqs.q: When does the Hocking County Recorder stop taking documents?
faqs.a: At 3:30 p.m. on weekdays. The office stays open to visitors until 4:00, and the research room closes at 3:45.

faqs.q: Can I order a copy of a recorded deed by email?
faqs.a: Yes. Emailed copies cost $2 per page, and requests should arrive by 3:30 p.m. A copy printed at the office costs $1 per page.

faqs.q: Who collects the Ohio conveyance fee in Hocking County?
faqs.a: The county auditor. Section 319.54(G)(3) sets the larger of $1 or ten cents per $100 of value, and the auditor's calculator shows the figure with a parcel transfer fee.

faqs.q: Will the recorder write my deed or check my title?
faqs.a: No. The office says it cannot perform title searches, give legal advice or prepare documents, so leave those steps to a closing agent or attorney.
